coaching.overall_assessment: The 31.35-second sequence captures distinct climbing phases characterized by a sustained left-arm deep bend around 16.2–18.3 seconds (reaching 29.4° elbow flexion) and a series of brief, rapid right-arm flexions between 23.8 and 30.9 seconds. Lower-body data indicates active knee flexion (angles below 60°) across several intervals, corresponding with upward hip vertical velocity peaks up to +0.044.
strengths: Demonstrated static holding capacity on the left upper body, maintaining a deep bend interval for approximately 2.07 seconds between 16.22s and 18.29s.
Effective lower-body engagement and high-step usage, evidenced by deep knee flexion (e.g., left knee at 54.3° at 9.41s and 42.0° at 26.66s; right knee at 48.2° at 17.25s and 41.9° at 18.82s).
Rapid contact execution in the later phase (23.8s–30.9s), where right-arm deep bend intervals averaged only 0.21 seconds, suggesting quick transitions rather than fatiguing over-gripping.
improvements: Work on hip trajectory consistency: Negative hip vertical velocity spikes (notably -0.085 at 10.98s) suggest sudden drops or hesitation; focusing on continuous lower-body drive could yield smoother upward movement.

Address unilateral lock-off endurance: While the left arm sustained a 2.07-second hold, the right arm's longest deep bend was 0.63 seconds; incorporating balanced lock-off conditioning could improve stability when right-arm holds are required.

Coordinate arm pull with lower-body extension: At 17.25s, maximum left-arm flexion (29.4°) coincided with an extended left knee (161.0°) and flexed right knee (48.2°); practicing synchronized hip-driven extension may reduce excessive mechanical load on the pulling arm.
limitations: Frequent missing joint data (null values) for the right elbow between 6.27s and 15.68s, as well as multiple knee intervals, preventing a complete kinetic chain evaluation.
Lack of contextual wall data: Hold sizes, wall angle, hold orientations, and route grade are unknown, meaning joint angles cannot be conclusively labeled as optimal or sub-optimal technique.
2D landmark estimation from MediaPipe is susceptible to parallax and perspective distortion, which limits the precision of measured joint angles and hip velocity.
